7ber is not July.

In Latin church books you'll often see 7ber, 8ber, 9ber and Xber. They mean September, October, November and December.

Why? The old Roman calendar started the year in March, so September was month seven (septem), October month eight (octo), and so on.

Every baptism record holds the same five facts: the date, the child, the parents, the godparents and the village. Find the date first and the rest falls into place.

One small trick, and a 130-year-old record suddenly makes sense.
